protocol.hypothesis: Earlier interpretation of public information can reduce time until useful physical aid, compared with competent finite conventional review.
protocol.fairness: Same raw public bytes, metadata, directory, formal-report delay, consented stock, fleet, field checks, dispatch reviews and physical world. Neither controller receives evaluator gold. Explicit structured requests and repost grouping are free in all arms.

references.B5: Conventional shared planner with free structured parsing plus finite human source review
references.B6: Real configured model perception, targeted confirmations and deterministic batching
references.B8: Stronger free broad keyword/location discovery, then the same targeted confirmations and batching
references.B9: Same configured model as a general tool-using disaster-response investigator: raw source batches, no specialized semantic preprocessor, same operational tools and reviewed physical response
references.B0: Extraction disconnected: formal observations only, same competent allocator

protocol.clocks: World travel/communication/review delays are modeled. Model availability is charged at max(declared latency, actual measured provider time). Human attention duration/workers are sensitivity parameters, not measured field productivity. SQL/HTTP wall overhead is separately reported, not sped up with the simulation clock.
protocol.negatives: Zero human-reading delay, immediate formal reports, failures, unserved needs and no advantage against a stronger keyword baseline must remain visible.
protocol.verification: Requests return a pending receipt. The same finite field queue progresses while owners review and trucks move; no controller must wait synchronously for all inquiries before acting on an already received need.
protocol.generalAgentScope: B9 is this explicit finite general-agent reference implementation, not all possible agents. It receives the same public sources, free structured parsing, approved policy, deterministic planner, owners, model configuration and total call/cost cap. The general agent chooses its own queries and drafts; no observer facts or specialized perception receipt are supplied.

manifest.reportingPolicy: Physical need at time zero; public source followed by the same delayed formal report for every arm. Source interpretation alone does not authorize a dispatch.
manifest.limitation: Internally authored synthetic cohort. Formal delay and human throughput require sensitivity tests; they are not field measurements.

collective.note: Operating hours alone are not useful service. Occupied shelter place-hours and finite water production are measured separately.

platformTransport.note: Actual platform peer HTTP is charged by the laboratory transport adapter; this is distinct from source-system messages.

information.note: These counts cover source-world claims only, not claims in an external platform database. Workflow acknowledgments are not semantic accuracy. Platform precision/recall requires matched external claims and independent task annotations.

firstUsefulServiceMs.note: First physical positive contribution to outstanding demand; partial service counts here, but not as sufficient service. Report firstUsefulRightCensored separately.

sufficientServiceMs.note: Sufficient physical service, completed positive-demand cases only; report right-censored cases alongside these percentiles.

needToServiceMs.note: Sufficient physical service, completed positive-demand cases only; report right-censored cases alongside these percentiles.

episodes.note: A new outstanding shortfall after coverage or retirement starts a new episode. Earlier aid is retained in history, never credited as response to a new episode. Withdrawn episodes are censored at withdrawal and must be reported separately; native resource quantities and integrals are not summed across types.

sourceCoverage.note: Source counts and inferred claims are not the number of people or needs physically served.

steps.detail:
The focus need for 70L of water at building `b17` (`7f8ae859c62ff6378d26ce3b`) is currently contested by an unverified signal (`6291568fc2653d420b1697a6`) claiming the site has been evacuated and supplies are complete. I have initiated a field verification (`inspection-23`) to resolve this contradiction.

Initial attempts to allocate resources for this and other water needs returned no feasible assignments with the currently available fleet. This may be due to vehicle positioning or existing commitments. I will monitor the verification of `b17` and continue to evaluate transport options for the remaining water and blanket needs.

**Pending:**
- Field verification of `b17` to confirm if the water need is still active.
- Re-evaluation of vehicle capacity and routing for unserved needs.
